title: Newton's Laws & Friction on Inclined Plane
description: Explore force resolution (gravity, normal, static & kinetic friction, external pulling force) on an inclined plane
fPull_desc: External force parallel to plane (positive: uphill, negative: downhill)
initialPos_desc: Initial distance from base of incline in meters
muS_desc: Maximum static friction threshold between surface and block
muK_desc: Kinetic friction coefficient during sliding motion
realEffectMass: In real mode, aerodynamic drag adds velocity-dependent resistance
realEffectFriction: Generates surface contact resistance against motion

formulas.netForceExpl: The resultant of applied pull, parallel gravity component, and friction dictates block acceleration.
formulas.normalExpl: The inclined surface supports the perpendicular weight component via normal force N.
formulas.frictionExpl: If driving force is below maximum static friction, the block remains stationary; once moving, kinetic friction opposes velocity.
formulas.criticalExpl: Without external force, the critical angle where sliding begins satisfies tan(θ) = μs.

steps.step1Title: Step 1: Discover Critical Angle of Sliding
steps.step1Instr: Select the 'Critical Angle' preset. Slightly adjust the angle slider to witness static friction overcome.
steps.step1Hint: At the critical threshold, tan(θ) = μs.
steps.step2Title: Step 2: Compare Simulated vs Theoretical Acceleration
steps.step2Instr: Select 'Frictionless Slide' and compare measured acceleration with theoretical g·sin(θ).
steps.step2Hint: Without friction, acceleration is independent of mass.
steps.step3Instr: Run 'Pulling Uphill' and analyze how friction reverses direction when the block ascends.
steps.step3Hint: Friction always opposes the direction of velocity.
